title: What information should you keep private online?
examples: What should I not share online?
Is it safe to say my school online?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Okay to share online, or keep private?

explain.say: Imagine giving a stranger in the street a note with your address, your school and your password. You would never do that! But online it can happen by accident. Look at the board. Some things are fine to share.

explain.say: Your favourite food, a drawing you made, your first name and your hobbies are usually okay. They are fun and do not tell anyone where to find you. What would you share?

explain.say: Now look at the keep private group: your home address, your password, your school name, your phone number and where you are right now. These could help a stranger find you. Which surprised you?

faq.q: What should I not share online?
faq.a: Keep private your full name with your address, school, phone number, passwords, and where you are right now. Ask a trusted adult if you are not sure.
asks: Tell me about the Keep private

faq.q: Is it safe to say my school online?
faq.a: It is best not to. Your school name, or a photo of your uniform, can help a stranger find you.
asks: Can I post photos in my uniform?

faq.q: How do I make a strong password?
faq.a: Use three random words joined together, like TeaCloudTiger, and add a number if needed. Use different passwords for different apps.
asks: Tell me about the Long password

faq.a: Settings that choose who can see your posts and contact you. Set them to friends only, with help from a parent or carer.
asks: Tell me about the Private settings

faq.q: What is okay to share online?
faq.a: Things that do not show where you are, like your hobbies, a drawing, or your favourite book, especially on safe, age-right sites.
asks: Tell me about the Okay to share

facts: The UK National Cyber Security Centre advises making passwords from three random words.
Photos can contain hidden location data, so many safety experts advise turning off location sharing for camera apps.

quiz.say: Which is safe to share with people online?
quiz.why: Your favourite food does not help anyone find you or get into your accounts.

wrong.0: Your address shows where you live.

quiz.why: Three random words make a long password that is hard to guess.

wrong.0: Short number patterns are guessed in seconds.
wrong.2: "password" is one of the most guessed passwords.
